title.raw: Us and Them: Living in a Polarized World — Climate

shortTeaser.raw: Climate change is real, and it is dangerous. Some people are actively trying to stop it.

teaser.raw: Climate change is real, and it is dangerous. Some people are actively trying to stop it. Others deny or intensify it – or suppress information. Most don’t bother at all and continue to contribute to global warming through their lifestyle.

title.raw: Arts and climate - exhibitions in Berlin and Madrid

shortTeaser.raw: Art exhibitions in Berlin and Madrid force visitors to rethink their own impact on the environment.

teaser.raw: Art exhibitions 'Down to earth' in Berlin and 'Moving Off the Land' in Madrid highlight the positive impact that months of coronavirus disruption has had on the environment. Curators want us to reflect on how we might move forward - and force people to rethink their own impact on the environment.

title.raw: We need to talk – about climate change

shortTeaser.raw: Why media coverage on global warming often leaves viewers cold.

teaser.raw: When Jeff Bezos took a joyride into space in 2021, US media dedicated 212 minutes of coverage to it in a single day. By comparison, they spent 267 minutes reporting on climate change - in a whole year! Clearly the media have a long way to go in reporting on the climate crisis.

shortTeaser.raw: Climate change especially impacts women's lives. In order to become decision makers, they need to organize themselves.

teaser.raw: Climate change often affects women more severely than men. But their situation usually improves if they organize themselves. To create fundamental change though, women from all socioeconomic groups must take part.
